# bugs #4228: Internal error for a constexpr or compound literal initializer with _Generic or a constant ?:

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4228/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch in place of the one attached to the ticket and close.
- Patch: [bugs-4228.patch](../../patches/bugs-4228.patch), commit [`8f3f9cc03`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/8f3f9cc038e74bff2ce8f87563f99171de9a48b7). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For `constexpr int object = _Generic (1, int: 1, default: 1.0);` the compiler reports error 47 for
an assignment from type `void`, and then a `validateLink` internal error or SIGSEGV. The defect
needs neither `_Generic` nor C23. `constexpr int object = 1 ? 2 : 3;` and the compound literal
`(int){1 ? 2 : 3}` fail in the same way, and the bit-field declaration `int a : 1 ? 3 : 4;` is
rejected as not constant. The reporter names mcs51 among five ports that fail. It was reproduced
for mcs51 with the two tests of this entry.

## Cause

`prepareDeclarationSymbol` in `src/SDCCsymt.c`, for `constexpr` objects, and the compound literal
rule in `src/SDCC.y` call `constExprTree (list2expr (sym->ival))`. `constExprTree` decorates the
tree and returns only a `bool`, so the tree that `decorateType` returns is lost. `decorateType`
replaces the root node for `_Generic` and for a conditional operator with a constant condition or
equal operands. The initializer list then points to the old root node, which is marked as
decorated and has no type, and the object is initialized from that node.

The bit-field rules in `src/SDCC.y` call `constExprValue` twice on one tree. The second call gets
the old root node.

## Fix

The new `constExprIlist` in `src/SDCCast.c` decorates the first expression of the list, stores the
tree that `decorateType` returns in the list, as `resolveIvalSym` does, and then calls
`constExprTree`. `prepareDeclarationSymbol` and the compound literal rule call the new function.
The bit-field rules call `constExprValue` once and use the value twice.

The patch attached to the ticket checks a copy of the tree and copies the list before each
evaluation of a `constexpr` object. This patch copies nothing.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4228.c` has 23 assertions on `constexpr` objects, compound literals,
and bit-field widths. `support/valdiag/tests/bug-4228.c` has eight cases. Two of them have an
initializer that is not constant and one has a negative bit-field width, and the compiler must
reject these. Without the patch the regression test does not compile for mcs51, and three of the
eight valdiag cases fail.

With the patch the regression test passes on the host, for six mcs51 configurations (the four
models, and small and large with `--stack-auto`), for stm8, and for z80. valdiag has no failures
for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The regression suite for mcs51-small has
no failures, and no other test changes its code size.

## Related

The patch does not fix these problems:

- The compiler terminates with SIGSEGV for `static constexpr int o = 2;` at block scope.
- `constexpr int m = 1 ? k : 0;` with a `constexpr` object `k` is rejected as not constant.
  Without the patch the compiler crashes on it.
- `case k:` with a `constexpr` object `k` is rejected as not constant.
- A `_Generic` expression without an association that matches, in a `constexpr` initializer,
  gets the correct error and then an internal error line.
